findings.title: Local Git reads are not specified as isolated from Git configuration
findings.detail: A clean process environment alone does not disable system, global, or checkout-local Git configuration. Git's URL rewrite and SSH-related settings can affect origin interpretation, and config can introduce behavior outside the stated fixed-command contract. The proposal explicitly rules out config/credential fallback, but does not say how Git configuration is disabled or isolated. This weakens the tokenless, local-only trust boundary and can make repository identity evidence misleading.
findings.minimal_fix: Specify and test hermetic Git invocation: disable system/global config and credential helpers, isolate HOME/XDG and repository config behavior, disable URL rewrites and external SSH/config hooks, and ensure no command can access a remote. Include hostile system/global/local config fixtures and assert no network/credential helper process starts.

findings.title: Administration authority intersection lacks a positive and negative test matrix
findings.detail: The design correctly requires acting-user administration, the current installation's administration grant, and metadata authority. The test task only calls out denied administration with zero runner calls; it does not require demonstrating that all three conditions are conjunctive or that a grant from a different installation/account cannot authorize the query. This leaves the central App/user isolation rule under-tested against the existing `RepositoryAccess` permission-intersection pattern (`src/SoFa.Modules.Workspace/Source/RepositoryAccess.cs:36-84`).
findings.minimal_fix: Add table-driven tests for each missing conjunct (user not admin, App installation lacks administration read, metadata missing), mismatched installation/repository, and the all-granted case. Assert denied cases make zero `/actions/runners` calls and only the current connected user's matching installation can authorize a successful query.

findings.title: Local and projected response bounds are qualitative rather than enforceable
findings.detail: The `.runner` file has a 32 KiB cap and GitHub has a 2 MiB transport/page-of-100 limit, but the local helper's aggregate stdin/stdout, checkout file/command output sizes, and final runtime response have no numeric limits. 'Bounded' and 'bound every file/command' do not define what the .NET bridge must reject or what coverage the UI reports. Existing routes enforce a 2 MiB projected-response bound (`src/SoFa.Modules.Workspace/WorkspaceModule.cs:208-210`), but this new endpoint has no corresponding planned requirement. Large configured inputs or projection overhead can therefore exceed memory/response expectations or be mistaken for complete evidence.
findings.minimal_fix: Set explicit maximum config/input bytes, per-file and per-command output bytes, helper stdout/stderr bytes, and serialized endpoint response bytes; reject/truncate only as unavailable/incomplete with original source coverage, never as empty or complete. Add boundary tests at and over each limit, including the final serialized response.

dimensions.name: Acceptance criteria
dimensions.evidence: The first-milestone registration, runner and committed-adoption scenarios are covered; response limits need explicit enforceable acceptance bounds (R57-3).

dimensions.name: Implementation completeness
dimensions.evidence: Tasks 1-4.4 cover implementation and integration; no implementation is claimed at this plan head.

dimensions.name: Tests
dimensions.evidence: Host/session/concurrency/source/browser tests are planned; the Git authority intersection matrix and numeric bound tests are missing (R57-2, R57-3).

dimensions.name: Quality checks
dimensions.evidence: Design 47 and task 4.3 require `npm run verify` and hosted CI; neither is represented as already run.

dimensions.name: Security
dimensions.evidence: Authority separation and owner-session cancellation are specified, but Git config isolation and full App/user intersection proof need work (R57-1, R57-2).

dimensions.name: Architecture / design conformance
dimensions.evidence: The proposal follows the accepted observer boundary in ADR-0006 and uses existing Workspace/session/source seams; implementation conformance remains future evidence.

dimensions.name: Documentation
dimensions.evidence: Task 4.2 requires architecture, README and configuration documentation updates.

dimensions.name: Product / spec consistency
dimensions.evidence: The proposal cites accepted product nodes and scopes the new capability to the owner-requested first milestone; future capacity, usage, process health and reservations are not claimed.

dimensions.name: Evidence
dimensions.evidence: The preflight is explicitly operator-read-only and not acceptance; actual acting-user GitHub evidence and final CI remain planned and limitations are stated.

dimensions.name: Human review
dimensions.evidence: Task 4.3 requires independent final-head review; protected approvals and owner decisions remain intact.

dimensions.name: Known limitations
dimensions.evidence: Future capacity/usage and unobserved process health are explicitly deferred; unknown coverage and owner-deferred phone rehearsal are not misrepresented.
